descriptions.tsh-managing-secrets: Secrets management patterns for cloud and Kubernetes environments. Use when implementing secure credential storage, secrets rotation, CI/CD authentication, or GitOps-compatible secret management.
descriptions.tsh-implementing-observability: Observability patterns for logging, monitoring, alerting, and distributed tracing. Use when setting up monitoring and alerting, implementing centralized logging, metrics collection, or distributed tracing across services, designing SLOs/SLIs and error budgets, or creating dashboards and runbooks.
descriptions.tsh-implementing-terraform-modules: Build reusable Terraform modules for AWS, Azure, and GCP infrastructure following infrastructure-as-code best practices. Use when creating reusable infrastructure modules, standardizing cloud provisioning, building multi-cloud compatible modules, or establishing organizational Terraform standards.
descriptions.tsh-implementing-backend: Backend service implementation patterns, standards, and procedures for Node.js, PHP, .NET, Java, and Go. Use when building REST/GraphQL APIs or CRUD endpoints with filtering and pagination (DataGrid), setting up authentication, database migrations and repository patterns, external service integrations, logging, Docker-based local development, OpenAPI documentation, testing strategies, or modular architecture with vertical slices.
descriptions.tsh-discovering-technical-context: Discover and establish technical context before implementing any feature. Prioritize project instructions, existing codebase patterns, and external documentation in that order. Use when starting any feature or fix, before writing tests (unit, integration, E2E), before architectural decisions that affect existing code, or when onboarding to a new area of the codebase.
descriptions.tsh-implementing-ci-cd: CI/CD pipeline design patterns and deployment strategies. Use when designing new pipelines, implementing deployment strategies (rolling, blue-green, canary), setting up GitOps workflows, or configuring secure CI/CD credentials.
descriptions.tsh-optimizing-cloud-cost: Optimize cloud costs through resource rightsizing, tagging strategies, reserved instances, and spending analysis. Use when reducing cloud spending or meeting budget constraints, right-sizing resources from utilization data, implementing cost governance and tagging, or analyzing multi-cloud cost optimization opportunities.
descriptions.tsh-implementing-kubernetes: Kubernetes deployment patterns, Helm charts, and cluster management. Use when deploying applications to Kubernetes, designing Deployment, StatefulSet, or Job configurations, implementing auto-scaling (HPA, VPA, KEDA), creating or modifying Helm charts, setting up ingress, networking, and service mesh, or configuring resource requests, limits, and QoS.
descriptions.tsh-designing-multi-cloud-architecture: Design multi-cloud architectures using a decision framework to select and integrate services across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Use when designing multi-cloud strategies, migrating between cloud providers, selecting cloud services for a workload, avoiding vendor lock-in, or leveraging best-of-breed services from multiple providers.
descriptions.tsh-analyzing-codebase: Analyzes the codebase of a system: its dependencies, how the business logic is implemented, and where code is duplicated. Use when onboarding to an unfamiliar repository, mapping a system before a change, or producing a codebase analysis document.
descriptions.tsh-analyzing-implementation-gaps: Implementation gap analysis: verifies what has to be implemented, what is already implemented, and compares a plan with the current state of the system. Use when checking a plan against existing code or deciding what to create, modify, or reuse.
descriptions.tsh-analyzing-requirements: Analyzes a task description, expands its context, inspects the current state of the system in the context of the task, and gathers information from different sources to build a PRD or research document. Use when a task is missing requirements or context, or before planning a feature.
descriptions.tsh-designing-architecture: Designs the architecture that solves a given task and proposes solutions that follow best practices and standards. Use when a feature needs a technical design or an implementation plan before coding starts.
descriptions.tsh-extracting-tasks: Identify and structure epics and user stories from workshop materials (cleaned transcripts, Figma designs, codebase analysis, and other documents). Produces a business-oriented task breakdown with dependencies, assumptions, and open questions. Use when turning workshop materials into a structured epic and story breakdown.
descriptions.tsh-formatting-jira-tasks: Transform extracted epics and user stories into Jira-ready format following a benchmark template. Handles field mapping, formatting for Jira markdown compatibility, two-gate user review, and guidance for Jira issue creation via Atlassian tools. Use when an approved task list needs to be formatted for Jira.
descriptions.tsh-processing-transcripts: Clean raw workshop or meeting transcripts from small talk, filler words, and off-topic tangents. Extract and structure business-relevant content into a standardized format with discussion topics, key decisions, action items, and open questions. Use when a raw transcript needs cleaning before analysis.
descriptions.tsh-reviewing-task-quality: Analyze extracted epics and user stories for quality gaps, missing edge cases, and improvement opportunities. Runs domain-agnostic analysis passes, optionally enriches findings with Jira board context, and produces accept/reject suggestions that refine the task list before Jira formatting. Use when an extracted task list needs a quality review before formatting.
descriptions.tsh-writing-e2e-tests: E2E testing patterns, verification procedures, and CI readiness checklists using Playwright. Use when writing, debugging, or reviewing end-to-end tests, fixing flaky tests, creating Page Objects, or mocking external APIs.
